messages.author: 5c25b990ffcfc759
messages.subject: interpret/rescale lavPredict scores
parts:
Hello,

I conducted a confirmatory factor analysis with lavaan, i.e.,

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 ' 
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)

Now want to create a binary variable based on the predicted values of a latent variables visual, textual, and speed, using lavPredict(). The problem is that these variables are standardized (i.e., mean = 0). This makes it difficult to find the right cutoff point, as I want to dichotomize the score based on whether people score above or below a specific manifest score (i.e., an average score of "3" on the items in the HolzingerSwineford1939 example - but note that in my actual case, the ideal cutoff is whether people tend to agree or to disagree on the Likert-type scale that the model is based on). Is there a workaround for this kind of problem? Can I, for instance, somehow create an artificial latent score that is on the same scale as the manifest items and that I can interpret the same way?

Thanks,
Sara

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: interpret/rescale lavPredict scores
parts:
The common factor has no scale of measurement, and its scale along the real-number line is arbitrarily assigned.   If your binary indicator is based on the observed response scale, then it is a function of a composite from the indicators, not a function of a common factor in a CFA model.

If you are willing to make more restrictive assumptions (e.g., parallel measurement, equality of thresholds across items), then you could use SEM to specify a generalizability-theory model, which would allow you to evaluate the dependability (absolute reliability) of a composite using a designated cutoff score.
